newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends dull day mixed, nearbys weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends dull day mixed, nearbys weaker.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in quiet dealings on Monday, with speculative selling pressuring the nearby contracts, dealers said.

Industry-related buying toward the lows and keen interest in the May/July switch helped to stem losses, they added, and prevented the May contract from slipping through nearby chart support at 160.00 cents a lb.
"It was pretty featureless," said one trader. "But the switch interest kept it from tanking."

Most-active May coffee eased 0.20 cent per lb on the day, to end at 161.65 cents, after ranging between 163.50 and 160.00 cents. Spot March coffee fell 1.35 cents, to 173.45 cents, while the back months finished 0.75 lower to 3.05 higher.
The nearby March/May switch narrowed to 11.80 cent, up from 12.95 cents at the close Friday, while May/July widened to 6.50 cents from 5.95 cents the previous session.
With turnover on Monday reaching only an estimated 6,576 lots, down sharply from Friday's official tally of 11,369 lots, some traders said the market may be running out of some steam.
"I think a lot of people are tired of this market and want to wait to see what happens," one trader said. "People are looking for a correction before we can move higher."
Since the beginning of the year, coffee futures have surged some 50 percent on worries about tight supplies and poor Latin American crops.

Technically, traders said the May contract would face some light support at today's low of 160.00, with the next level seen at 157.00-156.00 and strong support noted at 154.00, a double bottom on the charts. On the upside, near-term resistance was seen at 163.50-164.00, then 168.50 and 173.00, May's life-of-contract high set last week.
